newsitem.title: USA: NHL-HAWERCHUK, HUNTER SPECIAL SELECTIONS AS EAST ALL-STARS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-HAWERCHUK, HUNTER SPECIAL SELECTIONS AS EAST ALL-STARS.

text.p: Centres Dale Hawerchuk of the Philadelphia Flyers and Dale Hunter of the Washington Capitals were added to the Eastern Conference All-Star roster Wednesday as special selections by NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman.

Left wing Tony Granato of the San Jose Sharks and defenceman Viacheslav Fetisov of the Detroit Red Wings were added by the commissioner Tuesday to the Western squad for the January 18 game in San Jose, California.

Hawerchuk, 32, was the top pick in the 1981 NHL draft by the Winnipeg Jets and won the Calder Trophy as top rookie in 1981-82 when he scored 45 goals and 103 points. He was his team's leading scorer for the first 11 years of his career, the first nine in Winnipeg and then two with Buffalo.

"Dale Hawerchuk has long been known as one of the NHL's classiest, most skilled players," Bettman said. "His milestone of 1,400 career points is a testament to his outstanding play over a long and successful career."
The 36-year-old Hunter, the NHL's active career leader in penalty minutes with 3,274, spent seven years with Quebec before being traded to the Capitals for the 1987-88 season.
He helped Washington to the playoffs in each of his eight seasons there and was named team captain in 1994-95. This will be his first All-Star appearance.

"Dale Hunter's selection to the Eastern Conference All-Star team is our way of recognising his hard work and dedication to the game over 17 NHL seasons," Bettian said. "He is a highly respected player."
